Locked up in Thailand

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
she signed for a package containing MDMDA and now she is serving life in a Thai prison, sharing a cell with 23 other women

Further information:
Ashley Oosthuizen was 21 year old when she was arrested in Koh Samui, Thailand for allegedly dealing drugs or MDMA specifically. The story leading up the night she was dragged to a secret interrogation room on the island is long and complicated, but in short:

Ashley is a small-town girl from George, South Africa. At 18 she goes to Thailand to teach English. She meets Tristian, a hot bad boy, at a full moon party and starts dating him. He is 15 years older than her, and according to Tristan Ashley has no idea that he is a renowned drug dealer. At this point Tristan had already been dealing drugs on the island for a few years, mainly using the dark web to get large quantities of pure MDMA at great prices. He was getting his drugs delivered to the school where he worked as a science teacher.
Ashley was a kinder garden teacher, but when she lost her job Tristan offered for her to take on a managerial role at his restaurant https://www.hotinthebiscuit.com/

COVID hits, Tristan then leaves the island and moves to the Ukraine to study medicine and Ashley is left working her ass off to keep the restaurant afloat on an island with no tourists. Tristan’s big clients start asking for him to keep dealing even though he isn’t on the island, so he starts working with a friend, Dave. The deal is, packages will be shipped to the restaurant, Dave will collect them and do the drug drop offs.
But one night Ashley signs for the package, as Dave wasn’t there, and within minutes she is then arrested and dragged off.

According to the family and documentation they have from lawyers they have hired since her arrest, Ashley was interrogated for hours with no translator or legal representative, she was then forced to sign a confession written in Thai.

Initially her family had contact with her, but then she was put into 28 days of isolation apparently due to COVID. They were then told she is a security risk so no letters or phone calls will be allowed. The last time anyone heard from her was December 2021. Until last week, when she video called her mom to say she is still alive.

What we have:
Ashley’s mom and dad
Tristan - the boyfriend, who confesses to being the drug dealer and that Ashley knew nothing
Ashleys Lawyer
Bestie from Thailand
The confession documents
Videos and photos from life in Thailand



Extra Budget Items:
Travel
sending details to Niks
Ballpark is 13k

LOCKED UP IN THIALAND SCRIPT

VOICE OVER: This is a story about love turned toxic, drugs, the dark web, and a dream to travel the world ending in the trauma of a Thai prison. At its centre: 23-year-old Ashley Oosthuizen

MOM: To imagine a girl like her in there, is unbelievable
did well in school, like the sports, culture and arts. She loved photography, dancing

CARLI
I remember I was stressing about my final project for photography
and she just came towards me blowing on my forehead. And I was like, What are you doing? And then she was like, It's just looks like your head is really full.
And I would like to clear up some space for you to think clearly.

VOICE OVER: In 2020 Ashley was arrested in Kho Samoa, Thailand, nearly 10000km from home. She was charged with international drug trafficking, after signing for a package containing 260grams of the drug, MDMA

MOM:
M: when did you first speak to her after the arrest and what did she say?
Mom: She just said, I'm not a criminal. I'm not a criminal. I don't belong here.
You don't know? Where do you go? It's not like catching them before falling into a swimming pool.

VOICE OVER: In August last year, Ashley was found guilty and sentenced to life or 50 years behind bars, which she is currently serving in Thailand

ASHLEY: sometimes it feels like everyone is far away, but I know the people that really care about me will always be there.

VOICE OVER: To understand how a young woman from George, in the Southern Cape, landed up in a Thai prison we need to go back 3 years. After finishing high school while living with her mom, Lynnette Blignaut, Ashley paid her own way to Thailand with her high school sweetheart

MOM: I didn't give her my blessing to go. Unfortunately
and I said to her that I'm not happy, but I can't stop her.

VOICE OVER: Carli Dippenaar and Ashley have been friends since they were in Primary school and stayed in touch after Ashley left for Thailand

CARLI: She and her mom had different views about various things, and I think she wanted to just break away from what she thought that she needed to be and become who she really is

VOICE OVER: Ashley’s relationship ended and she moved to the island of Koh Samoa, finding a job as an English teacher at an international school. It was around this time that she met this man, Tristan Nettles, at a party. He was 12 years older than her.

CARLI: I think she really did fall in love with him quickly
she kept saying about how big his dreams were and how she wanted to be a part of them

TRISTAN: Ashley is a really terrifically sweet, wonderful girl.
At that time, I was already living a very fine lifestyle
I was dating, you know, very, physically attractive and beautiful women that had lots of sexual experience and that knew how to carry themselves in the kind of atmospheres that I was oftentimes attending.
And Ashley was you know, like a fish out of water in that kind of environment.

CARLI
It wasn't like an exclusive. relationship from the beginning.
He wanted to keep experiencing new things.
I do think that he told her that she wasn't good enough and she needed to change. I think Tristan was controlling her

VOICE OVER: According to Tristan, he was already trafficking drugs on the island when he and Ashley started dating.

TRITSAN:
I spent the summer over on Kopanang going to all the parties, and I'd spend all night selling drugs to the to the ex-pats and the white people until I found the ones that owned the villas, the ones that owned the clubs and the ones that own the boats
I had really great drugs and I had really great prices because I was getting them from the Dark web.
And yeah, I was making obscene amount of money
I never told Ashley about my involvement in drugs. She was much too young and green behind the gills, and she was certainly never involved in selling drugs for me.

VOICE OVER: Tristan had a day job as a science teacher at Panyadee - a prestigious international school. Ordering his drugs online and paying for them WITH bitcoin, he would have them shipped directly to the school’s mail room. He says this had been going ON for two years before he met Ashley.
Meanwhile Ashley had lost her teaching job and was battling to find work, barely able to afford her rent.



CARLI:
I think on some level she did know what was happening with Tristan
I genuinely, think that she didn't know in what degree or even if he was a drug dealer, but that he was someone that had drugs in his possession that I do think that she was fully aware.

VOICE OVER: Tristan quit his job as a teacher and opened this restaurant, hot in the biscuit, to make legitimate money. He hired Ashley as the manager, to help her get a work permit and earn a basic income.
But COVID restrictions made it hard

TRISTAN:
The business, instead of making me tons of money, was costing tons of money
I was putting tremendous pressure on Ashley
I was having to continuously spend so much money that I was making to flow basically, you know, her, her lifestyle so that she could keep living in Thailand working at this gift shop. So I was I was very hard on her a. but she just loved me, you know

MOM: We would get into a fight at some stage
she would he trusts and would ask her
or tell her to ask a family for money.
And I was just keeping on telling her that, you know, unfortunately, I cannot
The way that she was acting was not. It wasn't my daughter. It really wasn't.

VOICE OVER: Needing more money, Tristan enlisted the help of a friend on the island, David Rensburg, and started importing drugs to hot in the biscuit

TRISTAN
The drugs would come to Dave and then Dave would meet those, those individuals that I supply to.
But we weren't successful because the first package came through, the three next ones were intercepted and then the last one was transit upon Ashley.

VOICE OVER:
And this is where Ashley’s nightmare began:
According to this police report, translated from Thai to English by Ashley’s local lawyers, on the 8th of October 2020, she signed for a package with Dave Rensburg’s name on it. The package contained 260 grams of the drug, MDMA. When the arresting officers questioned her, Ashley admitted knowing there were drugs inside but said they belonged to Mr. Tris Seth Nettles, and that he had arranged for the drugs to be sent. Throughout the investigation, says the document, the accused person pleaded not guilty to all charges
Lizelle Martin is part of the legal team that has lodged an appeal to the Thai supreme court on Ashley’s behalf



LIZELLE MARTINS
The parcel was addressed to Dave Young's often brilliant book
So during the trial and Ashley's arrest, David, at no point was he arrested or.
Subpoenaed at all. They only arrested her.

TRISTAN
Tristan where is David now
He is dead
When
He committed suicide last year

LIZELLE
my biggest issue is that her previous attorney knew exactly what has happened. Mr. Nicholls. Send him screenshots, confirmation telling him listen, this is how the deals wind
I bought these drugs. We rallied through the school. They gave that information to the police.
They didn't use the information. Why?

VOICE OVER
Lizelle Martin’s is part of the legal team that has lodged an appeal to the Thai supreme court on Ashley’s behalf

LIZELLE:
To be guilty of any crime. Doesn't matter which country you are in. They are always certain elements of a crime that a prosecutor must prove, in this specific case for international drug trafficking. They must prove that she bought those drugs, yet she must have had the means to do it.
Then, obviously she must have. She must know what is inside that package. Those are the most three most important elements of this crime.

VOICE OVER: Even though Ashley confessed to knowing what was in the package, and to attending parties with Tristan while he was dealing drugs, Martin says admissions made during Ashley’s interrogation aren’t admissible in court. That’s because she was never read her rights, there wasn’t a lawyer or translator present, and 15 Thai police officers attended her nine hour interrogation, meaning she was likely under duress and denied her constitutional right against self-persecution.

LIZELLE:
Do you believe Ashley knew that Tristan was a drug dealer?
maybe she had some kind of an idea. Does it make her guilty of international drug trafficking? No, it doesn't.


VOICE OVER: When Ashley was arrested, a phone was confiscated from Hot in the Biscuit. During her trial these messages, allegedly showing Ashley and Tristan discussing drugs deals were presented as evidence.

LIZELLE:
M: What about that text message encounter between what looked like Tristen and Ashley?
The biggest problem for me is that they could never prove that it was actually her phone. The phone belonged to Hot in the Biscuit. There was more than one employee. They've never arrested the other employee.
But the most important thing is, it's got absolutely nothing to do with a package. It does not constitute the crime that she was charged with

VOICE OVER: This appeal process can take anywhere between 14 and 18 months. But, every year the king of Thailand offers a certain number of prisoners a Royal Pardon, which can be a lighter sentence or an early release. Martins has requested a Pardon for Ashley, and hopes that it will be granted during the Chinese new year in April or the king's birthday in July

LIZELLE:
And I appreciate your confidence and it's encouraging. But this is Thailand we're talking about here. They do not take drug trafficking lightly.
They don't. They don't at all. But she's not guilty. she is just an innocent girl sitting in a prison.

VOICE OVER : In her letters to Tristan sent a few weeks ago, it seems Ashley is still in love with him, or holding onto this notion of love, despite all she’s been through.
On screen: I dreamt last night i was drowning …
You were guiding me up but I was quickly losing strength
Why couldn’t your strong arms save me

TRISTAN
M: You admitted that you weren't in love with Ashley. Would you say you love her now?
Yes, I love her person so, so much. So it just breaks my heart that people continue to keep her there
M: So turn yourself in? It was your drug business. She had nothing to do with it.
I'm not going to turn myself in to the same people that are responsible for keeping her there and for risking her death right now from sickness and ill health.
That's not how good guys prevail. What I will do is live my life in a way to gain the power and influence and resources to hold those people directly accountable. Directly accountable.

LIZELLE:
If South Africa had a prison, a prisoner transfer treaty with Thailand, and she could come and serve her time here at home. What kind of time are we talking?
We're going to talk about three or four.
M: Three or four years compared to life.
That's it.


ASHLEY
I just want to tell everyone, I really love you
It feels like it’s been so long since I have spoken to you

VOICE OVER: While Ashley’s parents do all they can to get her out. she is sharing a prison cell with 67 other women

Would you say you love her now? Yes, I love her person so, so much. So it just breaks my heart that people continue to keep her there M: So turn yourself in? It was your drug business. She had nothing to do with it. I'm not going to turn myself in to the same people that are responsible for keeping her there and for risking her death right now from sickness and ill health. That's not how good guys prevail. What I will do is live my life in a way to gain the power and influence and resources to hold those people directly accountable. Directly accountable. LIZELLE: If South Africa had a prison, a prisoner transfer treaty with Thailand, and she could come and serve her time here at home. What kind of time are we talking? We're going to talk about three or four. M: Three or four years compared to life. That's it. ASHLEY I just want to tell everyone, I really love you It feels like it’s been so long since I have spoken to you VOICE OVER: While Ashley’s parents do all they can to get her out. she is sharing a prison cell with 67 other women

metadata.Further information: Ashley Oosthuizen was 21 year old when she was arrested in Koh Samui, Thailand for allegedly dealing drugs or MDMA specifically. The story leading up the night she was dragged to a secret interrogation room on the island is long and complicated, but in short: Ashley is a small-town girl from George, South Africa. At 18 she goes to Thailand to teach English. She meets Tristian, a hot bad boy, at a full moon party and starts dating him. He is 15 years older than her, and according to Tristan Ashley has no idea that he is a renowned drug dealer. At this point Tristan had already been dealing drugs on the island for a few years, mainly using the dark web to get large quantities of pure MDMA at great prices. He was getting his drugs delivered to the school where he worked as a science teacher. Ashley was a kinder garden teacher, but when she lost her job Tristan offered for her to take on a managerial role at his restaurant https://www.hotinthebiscuit.com/ COVID hits, Tristan then leaves the island and moves to the Ukraine to study medicine and Ashley is left working her ass off to keep the restaurant afloat on an island with no tourists. Tristan’s big clients start asking for him to keep dealing even though he isn’t on the island, so he starts working with a friend, Dave. The deal is, packages will be shipped to the restaurant, Dave will collect them and do the drug drop offs. But one night Ashley signs for the package, as Dave wasn’t there, and within minutes she is then arrested and dragged off. According to the family and documentation they have from lawyers they have hired since her arrest, Ashley was interrogated for hours with no translator or legal representative, she was then forced to sign a confession written in Thai. Initially her family had contact with her, but then she was put into 28 days of isolation apparently due to COVID. They were then told she is a security risk so no letters or phone calls will be allowed. The last time anyone heard from her was December 2021. Until last week, when she video called her mom to say she is still alive. What we have: Ashley’s mom and dad Tristan - the boyfriend, who confesses to being the drug dealer and that Ashley knew nothing Ashleys Lawyer Bestie from Thailand The confession documents Videos and photos from life in Thailand
